'''Iqbal Hussain Qureshi''' ([[Urdu]]: اقبال حسين قریشی) (27 September 1937 – 8&nbsp;December 2012) {{small|[[Sitara-i-Imtiaz|SI]], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]}},<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences">{{cite news|title=Deceased Fellows|url=http://paspk.org/pages.php?id=26&page=4|access-date=15 December 2013|newspaper=Pakistan Academy of Sciences|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131215064650/http://paspk.org/pages.php?id=26&page=4|archive-date=15 December 2013}}</ref> best known as '''I.H. Qureshi''', was a Pakistani [[Nuclear chemistry|nuclear chemist]] and an [[:wikt:Emeritus|Emeritus]] professor of chemistry at the [[University of Karachi]].<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> Qureshi was the principal contributor of scientific understanding of various chemical elements: [[bismuth]], [[Cobalt-60|cobalt]], [[strontium-90|strontium]], [[Isotopes of thallium|thallium]], [[tritium]], iron, [[rubidium]], and [[zinc]].{{rp|1–68}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Qureshi |first1=Iqbal Hessain |title=Radiochemical Separation by Amalgam Exchange |date=1963 |publisher=United States Atomic Energy Commission, Technical Information Service Extension |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PXCXk2cEC48C |access-date=11 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Search for All Records {{!}} OSTI.GOV |url=https://www.osti.gov/search/author:%22Qureshi,%20I.H.%22 |website=www.osti.gov |access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref>

His career was mostly spent with the [[Government of Pakistan]] after leaving his research work at the national laboratories, and advising the government on nuclear policy issues. He pushed his influential role at the [[Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority|Nuclear Regulatory Authority]] (PNRA) and the peaceful applications of nuclear science.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> He spent many years as an educator and research scientist at the [[Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences|Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences]] in [[Nilore]] before taking a professorship at the [[Karachi University]].<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/>

==Biography==

Iqbal Hussain Qureshi was born on 27 September 1937 in [[Ajmer]], Rajasthan in [[British Indian Empire|India]] where he received his early education.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> Following the [[Partition of India]] in 1947, his family emigrated to [[Pakistan]] and settled in [[Hyderabad, Pakistan|Hyderabad]], [[Sindh]], where he matriculated from a public high school.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences">{{cite web|last=Butt|first=Noor M.|title=Obituary: Dr. Iqbal Hussain Qureshi|url=http://www.paspk.org/proceedings/50,%20No.1/384d3fd0Obituary%20Dr.%20Iqbal%20H.%20Qureshi.pdf|publisher=N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences|access-date=15 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620130135/http://www.paspk.org/proceedings/50,%20No.1/384d3fd0Obituary%20Dr.%20Iqbal%20H.%20Qureshi.pdf|archive-date=20 June 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a [[child prodigy]], being accepted at the [[Sindh University]] in his teenage years to study chemistry.{{rp|88–89}}<ref name="National Archives of Pakistan">{{Citation | last =Staff | title =Biographical Encyclopedia of Pakistan | place =Islamabad | publisher =National Archives of Pakistan | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=zWxmAAAAMAAJ&q=iqbal+hussain+qureshi+chemistry | id =zWxmAAAAMAAJ | year = 1970}}</ref> In 1956, he graduated with a Bachelor of Science (BSc) in chemistry from the [[Sindh University]] and was noted in newspapers for his top standing in his class, winning the silver medallion with his degree.{{rp|89}}<ref name="National Archives of Pakistan"/> He continued his studies at the Sindh University, and graduated in 1958 with a Master of Science (MSc) in chemistry with Gold medallion.{{rp|88}}<ref name="National Archives of Pakistan"/><ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />

After earning a scholarship from the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) in 1960, Qureshi went to the United States to attend the [[University of Michigan]] and graduated in 1962 with an MSc in [[nuclear chemistry]].{{rp|97}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Michigan |first1=University of |title=Commencement Programs |date=1962 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nT-fAAAAMAAJ&q=qureshi |access-date=11 May 2020 |language=en-us |format=googlebooks |chapter={{small|Master of Science}}}}</ref> He went to Japan for his doctoral studies, attending the [[University of Tokyo]] where in 1963 he defended his thesis, ''"Radiochemical separations by Amalgam exchange"'', which contained fundamental work on [[Amalgam (chemistry)|chemical amalgam]] applications in [[radiochemistry]].<ref>{{Citation | title =Nuclear Science Abstracts | place =Ann Arbor, Michigan | publisher =[[University of Michigan at Ann Arbor]] | series =1 | volume =17 | year =1963 | pages =4552 | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=ukohAAAAMAAJ&q=iqbal+hussain+qureshi+ | id =ukohAAAAMAAJ }}</ref> In 1994, his biography was written and published by the [[University of Michigan]] in ''American Men & Women of Science: A Biographical Directory of Today's Leaders in Physical, Biological, and Related Sciences'' journal.{{rp|12}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kalte |first1=Pamela M. |last2=Nemeh |first2=Katherine H. |last3=Schusterbauer |first3=Noah |title=American Men & Women of Science: A Biographical Directory of Today's Leaders in Physical, Biological, and Related Sciences |date=2005 |publisher=Thomson Gale |isbn=978-0-7876-7398-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tf09BCmodB0C&q=iqbal+hussain+qureshi+PhD+tokyo+1963 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1967, Qureshi returned to the United States and briefly worked for the US [[National Bureau of Standards]] as a postdoctoral researcher before leaving for Denmark in 1969.{{rp|210}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sciences |first1=Pakistan Academy of |title=Proceedings of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences |date=1995 |publisher=Pakistan Academy of Sciences. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XbLaAAAAMAAJ&q=iqbal+hussain+qureshi+Denmark |language=en}}</ref>{{rp|96}}<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> In Denmark, he received training in the areas of uranium and plutonium [[isotope separation]], which was vital when he returned to Pakistan in 1971 with his expertise and knowledge.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />

===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission===

In 1960, Qureshi found employment with the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), and was posted to the Atomic Energy Center in Lahore where his interest built in [[radiochemistry]].{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt">{{cite web |title=Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt |url=http://paspk.org/wp-content/uploads/proceedings/50,%20No.1/384d3fd0Obituary%20Dr.%20Iqbal%20H.%20Qureshi.pdf |publisher=Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt |access-date=12 May 2020}}</ref> Upon returning to Pakistan from Denmark in 1971, he joined the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] (the national lab) in [[Nilore]], working at the Nuclear Chemistry Division (NCD).{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt"/>

As early as 1972, Qureshi joined the team of scientists that began working on the [[equation of state]] of the [[radioactive decay]] element [[plutonium]], while he established the computerized radiation detection chemical analysis laboratories at the Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology in 1973.{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt"/> In 1974, Qureshi and his team was instrumental at the national laboratory when he was the first to confirm the detection of [[radiation emission]]s coming from [[Rajasthan]] in India. Hence, by using [[neutron activation analysis]], confirming [[Pokhran-I]] the first Indian [[nuclear test]], which India later announced was indeed conducted at the [[Pokhran]] Test Range.{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt"/> Notably, he led the team that [[Chemical equation|balanced the chemical equation]] required for the [[Exothermic reaction|exothermic]] [[Nuclear reaction|chemical reaction]] in [[nuclear fission|fission device]]s.{{rp|57–58}}<ref name="Printwise Publications">{{cite book|last=Rehman|first=Shahidur|title=Long Road to Chagai|year=1999|publisher=Printwise Publications|location=Islamabad}}</ref> By 1977, he discovered the technique for balancing the nuclear [[Q value (nuclear science)|Q-value]] and energy balance in a [[boosted fission weapon]].<ref>Dr. Iqbal Hussain Qureshi (I. H. Qureshi) was one of the leading scientists who were involved in the development of a nuclear weapon in the early 1970s. Qureshi had led NCD in the physio-chemical development of fissionable materials in the device. Qureshi had discovered the [[Lithium-6|{{nuclide|lithium|6}}]]+[[Hydrogen-2|{{nuclide|hydrogen|2}}]]→[[Helium|{{nuclide|helium|4}}]]+22.4&nbsp;[[electron volt|MeV]] equation for balancing the Q-value and energy balance in a fission device.</ref><ref name="Stanford Security Studies, an imprint of Stanford University Press"/>

Eventually, Qureshi headed the Nuclear Chemistry Division (NCD) at the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology which was responsible for the multi-stage chemical process that separated, concentrated and isolated plutonium from uranium.<ref name="Stanford Security Studies, an imprint of Stanford University Press">{{cite book|last=Khan|first=Feroz Hassan|title=Eating grass the making of the Pakistani bomb|year=2012|publisher=Stanford Security Studies, an imprint of Stanford University Press|location=Stanford, California|isbn=978-0804784801}}</ref> At NCD, he also played a supervisory role in developing the Analytical Chemistry Group comprising modern and state of the art analytical chemistry laboratories such as the Analytical Chemistry Laboratory, Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy lab, Emission Spectrography lab, Chromatography lab, Electrochemical Analysis lab and [[radioisotope production]] labs.{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt"/> The Analytical Chemistry Laboratory was later certified by the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA), and oversaw the successful commissioning of the [[Pakistan Atomic Research Reactor|PARR-III]] reactor that went 'phase critical' {{clarify |date=May 2020}} in 1973.{{rp|96}}<ref name="Eulogy by Dr. NM Butt"/>

Qureshi engaged in research about [[copper-nickel]] alloys after introducing the [[Lattice dynamical system|lattice dynamical]] method to evaluate the [[copper|Cu<sub>29</sub>]]/[[Nickel|Ni<sub>28</sub>]] alloys.<ref name="IAEA Seminar on Effective Utilization and Management of Research Reactor">{{cite journal|last=Qureshi|first=Iqbal Hussain|author2=Naeem Ahmad Khan|title=Pakistan Research Reactor and its utilization|journal=IAEA Seminar on Effective Use and Management of Research Reactor|date=11 November 1983|volume=1|issue=1|url=http://www.iaea.org/inis/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/18/042/18042468.pdf|access-date=15 December 2013}}</ref> Key and fundamental research on understanding [[neutron flux]] was carried out by Qureshi, for which he managed to secure patents from the IAEA.<ref name="IAEA Seminar on Effective Utilization and Management of Research Reactor"/> After the conclusion of the Pakistan's [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|clandestine atomic bomb projects]], he was appointed chief technical officer at the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) in 1991; though he was more eager to return to academia.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />

Throughout his time at PAEC, Qureshi earned several scientific honors, including the Gold Medal and a [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|Fellowship of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] in 1994. He was a recipient of the [[Sitara-i-Imtiaz]] (Star of Excellence) from the [[Government of Pakistan]] in 1992.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> In 1997, from the Iranian Government, he received the [[Khwarizmi International Award]] for advancing and understanding the "Nuclear analytical techniques development and application in Pakistan".<ref name=IROST>{{cite web|last=IROST|title=Khwarizmi International Award 10th Session – 1997|url=http://www.irost.org/kia/content/khwarizmi-international-award-10th-session-1997|work=Khwarizmi International Award Committee|publisher=IROST|access-date=15 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215095928/http://www.irost.org/kia/content/khwarizmi-international-award-10th-session-1997|archive-date=15 December 2013}}</ref>

===Academia and government work===
In 1996, Qureshi retired from PAEC as Chief Scientific Officer and was made [[Emeritus Professor|scientist emeritus]], which allowed him to continue research at PINSTECH before moving to Karachi.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> He took up the professorship of chemistry at the [[Karachi University]] and headed the nuclear chemistry section at the [[H.E.J. Research Institute of Chemistry]]. During this time, he authored several articles and published books on nuclear chemistry. He retained his position till 2001 when he joined the [[Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority]] (PNRA).<ref name="Daily Times">{{cite journal |last =(NTI) |first=Nuclear Threat Initiative |author-link=Nuclear Threat Initiative |title=Pakistan is safe from hazards of radioactive rays: experts |newspaper=[[Daily Times (Karachi)|The Daily Times]] |publisher=Jang News Group |date=4 March 2008 |page=7 |volume=43 |url=https://www.nti.org/media/pdfs/pakistan_nuclear.pdf |access-date=31 May 2020 |format= summary, PDF |via=nti.org}} ([http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/default.asp?page=2008\03\04\story_4-3-2008_pg7_43 ''Original news link''])</ref>

At PNRA, Qureshi served as the chief scientific officer and adviser to the government on nuclear policy issues.<ref name="Associate Press of Pakistan">{{cite news|last=Staff agencies |title=Pakistan is safe from radioactive effects |url=http://www.app.com.pk/en_/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=30674&Itemid=2|access-date=15 December 2013|newspaper=Associate Press of Pakistan|date=4 March 2008|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215103750/http://www.app.com.pk/en_/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=30674&Itemid=2|archive-date=15 December 2013}}</ref> His contribution and policy efforts led to the physical security of the commercial [[Nuclear power in Pakistan|nuclear power]] infrastructure in the country and helped launched the nuclear awareness campaign following the [[2011 Fukushima I nuclear accidents|Fukushima nuclear disaster]] in 2011.<ref name="Nuclear Threat Initiatives">{{cite news|title=NTI Pakistan nuclear awareness|url=http://www.nti.org/media/pdfs/pakistan_nuclear.pdf?_=1316466791|access-date=15 December 2013|newspaper=Nuclear Threat Initiatives}}</ref> He served until 2009 when he decided to accept the professorship of chemistry at the [[Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences|Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences]]. In December 2012 Qureshi had a sudden breathing problem and died. He is buried in [[Karachi]], Sindh.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />

===Personal life and interests===

In Pakistan's academia and [[Pakistan Nuclear Society|nuclear society]], Qureshi was well known for his interests in classical [[music theory]] and love of playing the guitar and [[sitar]], which he played on several occasions.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> He also had an interest in [[American poetry]], which he often quoted among his peers while working on the bomb program, and played tennis avidly during his later life.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> He was married twice; his first wife died in the 1980s and he later remarried.<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> He had two sons, one a [[neurosurgeon]] while the other is a [[computer scientist]].<ref name="N.M. Butt, Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />
